_note: Q1FY27 ACTUALS for the four integrated steel mills, so P4 can grade the
commitments in steel_guidance.json rather than withhold on 'no actual'.
WHY THIS IS A SECOND FILE. Loading the commitments alone left guidance still
withheld, with the reason changing from 'no open guidance' to 'no actual' —
because run_scores does NOT use load_guidance's confidence model. It uses
guidance_runrate.score_entity, which is run-rate arithmetic: actual versus
target, weighted by how much of the period has elapsed. That replaced a
hand-weighted evidence vote on 2026-08-20 precisely because the old version
never read target_value and let 'guidance reiterated' drift confidence upward.
So P4 needs BOTH sides cited: the commitment AND the print.
EVERY NUMBER HERE IS ALREADY IN base_financials.yaml, where it built each
name's base_ebitda, and every one reconciles on the volume x EBITDA/t
identity against the cited absolute print — the cross-check steel has and
aluminium does not:
sail          4.16 mt x  9,974 = Rs 4,149 cr  vs cited Rs 41.5 bn
jindal_steel  2.20 mt x 12,000 = Rs 2,640 cr  vs cited Rs 26.7 bn
tata_steel    5.17 mt x 18,199 = Rs 9,409 cr  vs consol Rs 93.7 bn
JSW'S VOLUME IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT. Its 24.84 mt in steel.yaml is DERIVED
from EBITDA/t against absolute EBITDA, not cited — and an `actual` that P4
grades a commitment against must be a number someone actually said. This is
SILENT_BUGS entry 6 exactly: a quote that explains HOW a figure was arrived
at rather than stating it means the figure is derived, and a derived actual
wearing a citation is the failure that entry records. JSW's EBITDA/t IS
cited, so that one is here and the volume is not.
WHAT WILL STILL WITHHOLD AFTER THIS, AND CORRECTLY:
tata_steel  margin:Q2FY27, cost_per_t:Q2FY27  — Q2 has not happened. A
guide issued for a future quarter SHOULD have no actual.
tata_steel  capex:FY30                        — four years out.
jindal      ebitda_per_t:FY28                 — two years out.
jsw_steel   its only commitment is status='missed', so it is not OPEN and
does not score the pillar. It still builds the track record,
which is the point of resolving it.

FIVE OF SIX QUOTES WERE MIS-ATTRIBUTED IN THE FIRST DRAFT — the dates were taken from the candidate scan's grouping rather than checked against the file, and one failed on CHARACTER not date: the Tata line uses the rupee SIGN (₹2,950/t, ₹18,200/t) where the draft wrote 'Rs'. A substring check against each cited digest caught all five; the schema would not have, because it only enforces that a quote is non-empty. Same gap as SILENT_BUGS entry 6. The bad rows were DELETED from `observations` and reloaded rather than left beside the corrected ones, because the loader's idempotency key is the quote text, so a corrected quote inserts a second row instead of replacing the first.
